instruction.text: This is a map showing the continents of the world. Select the image that shows South America.

atoms.b: South America is made up of 12 countries, with a ((++population popularity)) of roughly 440 million people.
South America is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the ((++east south)) and the Pacific Ocean to the ((north ++west)).
It is also connected to North America via a natural ((water ++land)) bridge, known as the Isthmus of Panama.

hint.text: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land with water on both sides that connects two larger pieces of land.
hint.label: Isthmus

hint.label: Imaginary lines
hint.text: The Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn are imaginary lines circling the Earth. The Equator is in the middle and divides the globe into its Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The Tropic of Capricorn is located just south of the Equator.

atoms.text: South America is located in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Due to its sheer length and size, it contains nearly all the world’s major climate zones.
Most of the northern and central regions around the Equator have a tropical climate, with wet and dry seasons and hot, humid weather all year round.
Moving past the Tropic of Capricorn, you can find many regions with a dry climate. These include warm, grassland plains, as well as the driest hot desert on Earth.
The southern regions mostly have a temperate climate, with four distinct seasons. In the continent’s southernmost areas, the climate becomes much colder as it nears the polar zone.

atoms.b: Humans have lived in South America for over 14,000 ((days ++years)), so it is home to hundreds of indigenous tribes and native languages.
However, due to colonialism, European languages are official languages in every South American ((++country island)), with Spanish and Portuguese being the two most commonly spoken.
The United Kingdom, France and the Netherlands also still have overseas territories in ((++South North)) America.

hint.text: An overseas territory is an area of land that is owned or politically controlled by a country far away from it. While these areas belong to other countries, they each have their own distinct cultures and often different languages, laws and currencies too.
hint.label: Overseas territories
